recipes.title: Quick Mozzarella for Neapolitan Pizza
recipes.source_note: cheeseforum.org - decadentcookie
recipes.description: A quick mozzarella recipe using citric acid, designed for high-heat pizza baking.

instructions.text: Dilute citric acid in 125ml water. Add to cold milk and stir well.
Heat milk to 90°F (32°C). Dilute rennet in 1/4 cup cool water.
Add rennet to milk, stir gently for 30 seconds. Let set until clean break (about 5-10 min).
Cut curds into 1-inch cubes. Let rest 5 minutes.
Slowly heat curds to 105°F (40°C) while stirring gently.
Drain curds in colander for about 5 minutes.
Heat water to 185°F (85°C). Place drained curds in colander and submerge in hot water for 1 minute.
Remove curds and knead, folding corners inward to smooth. Repeat heating and kneading 5 times total.
Add salt during the final two kneading repetitions.
Shape into balls and immediately place in ice water to set shape.
For pizza use: salt the mozzarella and place between paper towels with a plate on top to reduce moisture before baking.

notes: Non-homogenized milk produces better texture
If mozzarella doesn't stretch well, check milk freshness and acidity
For better melting on pizza, try traditionally cultured mozzarella instead

missing_inputs: 4 L whole milk (3.25% recommended, non-homogenized preferred)

recipes.title: Halloumi Cheese (Basic Method)
recipes.source_note: cheeseforum.org
recipes.description: Traditional Cypriot cheese that can be grilled or fried without melting. Simple recipe requiring no starter culture.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 90°F (32°C). Add rennet and stir gently.
Wait approximately 30 minutes until milk sets firmly.
Break up curds and place into muslin cloth in two portions.
Drain whey back into pan. Let curds stand in muslin for about 30 minutes.
Heat the collected whey to boiling point (212°F/100°C).
Remove soft curds from muslin and place into the boiling whey.
Simmer gently for approximately 20 minutes until cheese floats to top.
Remove cheese, sprinkle with salt if desired, fold in half while still warm.
Apply weight on top and refrigerate for at least 2 hours.
Store in jar with small amount of whey, kept cool.

notes: Sheep milk yields about 1 kg cheese from 4 liters; cow milk needs 9 liters for same yield
No starter culture required - this is a forgiving cheese
If pH drops below 6 before boiling, texture will suffer
Target salt level: 1.5-2% based on taste preference
Halloumi won't melt when grilled due to its high pH

missing_inputs: 8 pints fresh milk (goat, sheep, or cow)

recipes.title: Traditional Feta Cheese
recipes.source_note: cheeseforum.org - Cheese Head
recipes.description: Classic Greek-style brined cheese. Longer aging produces more crumbly texture.

instructions.text: Warm milk to 85°F (29.5°C).
Add starter culture and mix thoroughly with a whisk until uniform.
Allow milk to ripen for 2 hours at 85°F.
Dissolve rennet in 3-4 tablespoons cool water (hot water destroys rennet).
Pour rennet slowly into milk while stirring constantly for at least 5 minutes.
Allow milk to set 1-2 hours until firm curds form with a clean break.
Cut curds into 1/2 inch cubes using a long knife.
Let curds rest 10 minutes, then cut any larger pieces.
Allow curds to sit 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Drain whey by pouring through a cheesecloth-lined colander.
Tie cloth corners and hang to drain for 5 hours.
Transfer cheese to rectangular container (about 1 inch thick) and refrigerate 90 minutes.
Remove and cut into 1-inch cubes.
Prepare brine: dissolve 1.5 cups salt in 1 quart warm water, then cool.
Place cheese cubes in COLD brine solution and refrigerate for 5-30 days.
Pat dry with paper towel before serving. Store in airtight container.

notes: Longer brining (up to 30 days) produces more crumbly, tangy feta
If using cow milk, add lipase for more authentic piquant flavor
Raw milk requires minimum 60 days aging for safety
Ultra-pasteurized milk will not work for this recipe

missing_inputs: 1 gallon fresh milk (cow, goat, or sheep)

recipes.title: Gouda Cheese
recipes.source_note: cheeseforum.org - Cheese Head
recipes.description: Classic Dutch washed-curd cheese with sweet, mild flavor. Can be aged from 4 weeks to over a year.

instructions.text: Warm milk to 85°F (29.5°C). Add starter culture and mix thoroughly.
Dissolve rennet in 3-4 tablespoons cool water, then stir into milk for 5+ minutes.
Allow milk to set 1-2 hours until firm curds form.
Cut curds into 1/2 inch cubes and let sit 10 minutes.
Gradually raise temperature to 102°F (39°C) over 45 minutes, stirring gently every few minutes.
Remove 3 cups whey and replace with equal amount of 102°F water. This is the 'washing' step.
Repeat whey replacement every 15 minutes for 45 minutes (three total replacements).
Drain whey through cheesecloth-lined mold.
Press at 20 lbs (9 kg) for 45 minutes.
Flip cheese and press at 40 lbs (18 kg) for 3 hours.
Prepare cold brine and float cheese for 3 hours, flipping every 45 minutes.
Pat dry and refrigerate for minimum 25 days, flipping daily.
Monitor for mold - treat with vinegar-dampened paper towels as needed.
Optional: wax cheese for extended aging (3+ months).

notes: The 'washing' step (replacing whey with water) removes lactose, creating Gouda's characteristic sweetness
Young Gouda: 4-8 weeks aging. Mature Gouda: 8-17+ weeks
Wax after 3 weeks of aging if planning long-term storage
Flora Danica culture adds buttery diacetyl notes
Higher pressing weights (up to 50 lbs) create denser texture

recipes.title: Traditional Cultured Mozzarella
recipes.source_note: cheeseforum.org
recipes.description: Authentic mozzarella made with thermophilic cultures for superior flavor and melt. Takes longer but produces better results than quick methods.

ingredients.item: thermophilic culture C201 (ST, LB, LH strains)

instructions.text: Heat milk to target temperature: 32°C (90°F) for softer mozzarella, or 37°C (99°F) for firmer pizza-style.
Add thermophilic culture and yogurt. Mix well.
Add lipase if desired for more traditional flavor.
Let culture ripen for 1 hour before adding rennet.
Add diluted rennet and stir gently for 1 minute.
Allow to set until clean break (40-60 minutes).
Cut curds into 1/2 inch cubes.
Let curds rest, then slowly heat to 40°C (104°F) over 30 minutes.
Monitor pH - target 5.2-5.4 before stretching.
Drain curds and let acidify until stretchy when tested in hot water.
Heat water to 170-180°F (77-82°C). Stretch curds in hot water, kneading until smooth and glossy.
Shape into balls and cool in ice water or light brine.

notes: 32°C produces softer mozzarella for fresh eating (caprese, etc.)
37°C produces firmer mozzarella better suited for pizza
The 1-hour culture ripening before rennet is key for flavor development
Test stretch readiness: a small piece in hot water should stretch without breaking
Cultured mozzarella melts better than quick citric acid versions

recipes.title: Queso Panela (Mexican Fresh Cheese)
recipes.source_note: cheeseforum.org
recipes.description: A mild, white Mexican cheese that softens when heated but doesn't melt. Perfect for grilling or frying.

instructions.text: Pour milk into pot. Dissolve powdered milk over medium heat without boiling.
Dilute calcium chloride in 1/4 cup boiled water and add to warm milk, stirring well.
Remove from heat. Dissolve rennet in 1/4 cup water and add to milk, stirring gently.
Let stand for 20 minutes to form curd.
Cut curd into 1-inch cubes. Let rest 20+ minutes.
Heat gently while stirring.
Strain whey through cheesecloth-lined colander.
Add salt to curds and knead lightly.
Place in colander with cheesecloth, apply weight, and press for several hours, turning halfway.
Once cheese releases no more whey, store in airtight container in refrigerator.

notes: Shelf life approximately 15 days refrigerated
Softens when heated but doesn't melt - ideal for grilling
Milk powder increases protein content for better curd formation

recipes.title: Spiced Paneer (Indian Fresh Cheese)
recipes.source_note: cheeseforum.org
recipes.description: Traditional Indian cheese with jalapeño and cumin, perfect for curries or pan-frying.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 180-190°F (82-88°C).
Hold milk at temperature for 20-30 minutes.
Add citric acid or lemon juice slowly while stirring. Curds should form immediately.
Once curds separate clearly from whey, remove from heat.
Drain through cheesecloth-lined colander.
Mix salt, jalapeño, and cumin into drained curds.
Place curds between two dinner plates.
Add heavy weight and refrigerate for 4-6 hours.
Cut into cubes for cooking.

notes: Longer pressing creates firmer cheese
Can substitute lime juice for lemon juice

recipes.title: Appenzeller Swiss Cheese
recipes.source_note: cheeseforum.org
recipes.description: Traditional Swiss-style cheese with a washed rind, aged minimum 1 year. Includes detailed pH targets for consistent results.

instructions.text: Heat milk to ~90°F. Target starting pH: 6.75
Add cultures and ripen. Add rennet when pH drops ≥0.1
Allow flocculation (25-35 minutes).
Cut curds to 1/8 inch. Maintain pH 6.35 at whey pitch.
Cook curd to ~120°F over 60 minutes (max 1°F per minute).
Pitch curds for 5 minutes.
Press in warm whey: 1 hour with low weight, flipping 2-4 times.
Press outside whey: 40 min at 25 lbs, 1 hr at 25 lbs, 2 hr at 50 lbs, 4 hr at 50 lbs.
Brine: 6 hours per pound at 18% salt. Target pH in brine: 5.4
Air dry 12 hours, then age at 50-55°F, 80-85% humidity.
Wash daily for 2 weeks, then weekly for 2 months.
Age minimum 1 year for full flavor development.

notes: pH targets: Start 6.75 → Whey pitch 6.35 → Brine 5.4
Add 5g CaCl2 + 5ml white vinegar per gallon to brine
Washed rind develops during aging
Minimum 1 year aging for authentic flavor

recipes.title: Cheddasiago (Cheddared Thermophilic Cheese)
recipes.source_note: cheeseforum.org
recipes.description: Experimental cheese combining Asiago's thermophilic cultures with cheddar's cheddaring process.
recipes.servings_yield: About 1 lb 13 oz from 9 liters milk

instructions.text: Combine milk and cream for ~3.8% butterfat.
Heat to 95°F. Add cultures and ripen 30 minutes.
Add rennet. Wait for clean break.
Cut curds to 3/8 inch cubes.
Gradually raise temperature to 115°F over 45 minutes with gentle stirring.
Continue stirring until curds reach pea size and pass grip test.
Drain whey. Consolidate curds into 1-inch thick layer.
Cheddar: Place warm water on curds for 15 minutes. Repeat 4 times over 1.5 hours, targeting pH 5.3.
Mill curds, add salt, mix well.
Press: 30 lbs increasing to 170 lbs overnight.
Air dry 2-3 days at 55°F.
Wax in red coating. Age minimum 3 months (6+ recommended).

notes: Target pH 5.3 after cheddaring
Red wax is traditional for visual appeal
Longer aging (6+ months) develops more complex flavor

recipes.title: Tvorog (Russian Farmer's Cheese)
recipes.source_note: CheeseForum.org - Fresh Cheeses (reconstructed from forum discussion)
recipes.description: A soft, fresh Russian-style cheese similar to quark. Mild, tangy, and versatile for sweet or savory dishes.

instructions.text: Heat milk to lukewarm (about 85-90°F/30-32°C) - it should feel neutral to the touch.
Stir in the buttermilk and mix well.
Cover and let sit at room temperature for 24-48 hours until the milk has thickened and set like yogurt.
Line a colander with cheesecloth or butter muslin and set over a bowl.
Gently pour or ladle the thickened milk into the lined colander.
Let drain for 2-4 hours for a creamy texture, or overnight for a drier, crumbly texture.
Season with salt if desired.
Transfer to a container and refrigerate. Use within 1 week.

notes: No rennet required - this is a purely lactic-set cheese
Use as you would ricotta or quark
Traditional in Russian blintzes (syrniki) and pierogi fillings
Can be sweetened with sugar for desserts

recipes.title: 18% Brine for Cheese Making
recipes.source_note: Little Green Cheese - littlegreencheese.com
recipes.description: A saturated salt brine solution used for brining cheeses like feta, gouda, and other aged varieties.

ingredients.item: non-iodized salt (sea salt or cheese salt)

instructions.text: Heat 1/2 gallon of water to dissolve the salt more easily.
Add salt gradually, stirring until fully dissolved. The solution should be saturated.
Add remaining water to cool the solution.
Add calcium chloride to prevent calcium leaching from cheese.
Add vinegar to lower pH and prevent bacterial growth.
Cool brine to 50-55°F before using.
Store in refrigerator. Brine can be reused multiple times.

notes: Check salinity with a brine hydrometer or egg float test
Brine time varies by cheese
Never use iodized salt

recipes.title: Tilsit (Washed Rind Cheese)

Drain whey and transfer curds to cheese mold.
Press at 10 lbs for 30 minutes, flip, then 20 lbs for 6-8 hours.
Brine in saturated salt solution for 8-12 hours.
Age at 50-55°F, 90% humidity. Wash rind every 2-3 days for first 2 weeks.
Continue aging 2-4 months, washing weekly.

Similar to Limburger but milder

recipes.title: English Coulommiers

instructions.text: Heat milk (and cream if using) to 90°F (32°C).
Sprinkle cultures and molds over surface. Stir in after 2 minutes.
Ripen for 90 minutes at 90°F.
Add calcium chloride if using, then diluted rennet.
Let set 90 minutes until very firm clean break.
Cut curds into 1-inch cubes. Let rest 5 minutes.
Gently ladle curds into Coulommiers molds.
Let drain at room temperature, flipping every few hours, for 24 hours.
Unmold and salt all surfaces lightly.
Age at 50-55°F, 90-95% humidity. Flip daily for first week.
White mold should cover cheese in 10-14 days.
Wrap in cheese paper when fully ripened. Best at 4-6 weeks.

notes: Coulommiers is essentially a larger, thicker Camembert
Best eaten at room temperature

recipes.title: Traditional Cheddar
recipes.source_note: Little Green Cheese - littlegreencheese.com
recipes.description: Classic English cheddar using the traditional cheddaring technique.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F (30°C). Add culture and ripen 45 minutes.
Add calcium chloride if using pasteurized milk.
Add diluted rennet. Let set 45-60 minutes until clean break.
Cut curds into 1/4-inch cubes. Let heal 5 minutes.
Slowly heat to 102°F (39°C) over 30 minutes, stirring gently.
Hold at 102°F for 30-45 minutes, stirring.
Drain whey to level of curds. Let curds mat for 15 minutes.
Cut curd mass into slabs. Stack and flip every 15 minutes for 2 hours (cheddaring).
Mill cheddared slabs into finger-sized pieces.
Add salt, mix thoroughly.
Pack into cloth-lined mold. Press at 10 lbs for 15 minutes.
Flip, press at 30 lbs for 12 hours. Flip, press 30 lbs for 12 more hours.
Air dry 2-3 days until rind forms.
Wax or bandage wrap. Age at 55°F for 3-12 months.

notes: Cheddaring develops the characteristic texture

recipes.title: Jarlsberg-Style Cheese

Let curds settle 5 minutes. Drain whey.
Transfer curds to mold. Press at 10 lbs for 30 minutes.

recipes.title: Mysost (Norwegian Whey Cheese)
recipes.source_note: Little Green Cheese - littlegreencheese.com
recipes.description: A sweet, caramel-flavored Scandinavian cheese made by reducing whey. Also known as Brunost.

instructions.text: Start with fresh, sweet whey from the same day's cheesemaking.
Pour whey into a large, heavy-bottomed pot. Add cream and milk if using.
Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, stirring occasionally.
Reduce heat to medium. Continue boiling and stirring as liquid reduces.
As volume decreases (2-3 hours), stir more frequently. Mixture will turn tan, then brown.
When reduced to about 1/4 volume and thick like caramel sauce, remove from heat.
Beat vigorously with wooden spoon for 5-10 minutes as it cools.
Pour into a buttered mold while still pourable.
Refrigerate until firm.

notes: Goat whey produces traditional Gjetost
Constant stirring prevents burning
Traditional Norwegian breakfast

recipes.title: Ricotta Salata

instructions.text: Combine whey and milk in a large pot. Heat to 200°F (93°C).

Remove from heat. Let sit 10 minutes.
Skim curds into cheesecloth-lined colander.
Let drain 30 minutes, then mix in salt.
Pack salted curds into a ricotta mold.
Press with 5 lbs weight for 12 hours. Flip and press another 12 hours.
Remove from mold. Rub exterior with additional salt.
Place on rack in refrigerator. Turn daily and salt lightly for 1 week.
Continue aging 2-4 weeks total.

notes: Salata means salted
Excellent crumbled over salads or pasta

instructions.text: Heat milk to 90°F (32°C). Add culture and ripen 45 minutes.

Add diluted rennet. Let set 45 minutes until clean break.

Slowly heat to 100°F (38°C) over 30 minutes.
Hold at 100°F, stirring, for 30 minutes.
Let curds settle 5 minutes. Drain whey.
Stir curds to release more whey. Add salt and mix.
Transfer to mold. Press at 10 lbs for 15 minutes.

recipes.title: Queso Fresco

Drain whey by hand, return curds to pot.

recipes.title: Kaffeost (Swedish Coffee Cheese)

recipes.title: Tzafatit (Cheese from Tzfat)

recipes.title: Camembert

recipes.title: Parmesan Cheese

recipes.title: Homemade Cheddar Cheese

recipes.title: Farmhouse Cheddar (18th Century Recipe)

recipes.description: Historical cheddar made without added cultures, relying on natural bacteria in raw milk. Produces a dry, grateable cheese similar to parmesan.

instructions.text: Warm milk to 85-90°F.

recipes.title: Traditional Cultured Mozzarella

recipes.description: Authentic mozzarella using natural starter culture rather than citric acid shortcut. Deeper, more complex flavor with proper stretch.

instructions.text: Heat milk to approximately 95°F (35°C).

recipes.title: Italian Havarti Cheese

recipes.description: A mild, creamy Danish-style cheese with Italian herb seasoning. Uses washed-curd technique and ages in just 4-6 weeks.

Gently stir 5-10 minutes to achieve uniform sizing. Continue stirring 5 additional minutes until curds resemble half a grape and feel like poached egg whites.

Drain whey completely. Add salt and Italian seasoning to pot. Leave covered 20 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes.
Add 1 gallon 105°F sterilized water, stir 1 minute, then let curds sit under whey 5 minutes.
Line cheese form with damp cloth and place in shallow baking dish. Pack curds into form.
Press at low pressure 30 minutes, then redress and press at medium pressure 5 additional hours.
Place on rack in plastic container. Flip daily, draining accumulated whey, for 2-5 days until surface feels dry.
Vacuum seal and age in temperature-controlled environment.

notes: Fresh raw milk no older than 2 days is recommended
Good after 4 weeks aging, 6 weeks recommended for raw milk cheese
Washed-curd technique creates characteristic creamy texture

Can be strained further to make cream cheese

recipes.title: Swiss Cheese
recipes.source_note: David Fankhauser - fankhauserblog.wordpress.com
recipes.description: Traditional Swiss with characteristic eyes (holes) created by Propionibacterium. An advanced cheese requiring precise temperature control through multiple aging stages.

ingredients.item: fresh yogurt (L. bulgaricus and S. thermophiles)

instructions.text: Warm milk to 95°F. Add cultures, set 20 minutes.
Dissolve rennet in cool water, stir into milk, wait ~30 minutes for clean break.
Make 1/8-inch vertical cuts, whisk to wheat-grain size curds.
Hold at 95°F for 30-40 minutes, then slowly raise to 125°F.
Maintain 125°F for 45 additional minutes.
Let curds settle, drain into cloth-lined hoop. Press 5 minutes.
Replace cloth, press 3 hours. Rinse cloth in saturated salt water and continue pressing for 9 more hours total (3-hour intervals).

FIRST AGING: 10 days at 50-55°F (90% humidity), wiping daily with salt-soaked cloth.
WARM ROOM: Move to 70°F (70-80% humidity) for 1.5 months. Wipe with clean salt water 2x per week. Cheese should puff up as holes form.
FINAL CURING: Age at 40-45°F for 4 months to 1 year.

recipes.title: Homemade Cottage Cheese
recipes.source_note: Seven Sons Farms - sevensons.net
recipes.description: Simple large-curd cottage cheese made with milk and vinegar. Ready in about an hour, creamy texture with optional heavy cream.

instructions.text: Pour one gallon of milk into a large pot and heat to approximately 190°F, stirring gently with a wooden spoon to prevent burning.

Add 3/4 cup of vinegar or lemon juice and stir. Cover the pot and let it rest for 30 minutes.
Line a colander with cheesecloth or a clean cotton towel and place it over a bowl.

Gather the cloth ends tightly, forming a ball. Run cold water over it while gently squeezing.
Place the cooled cheese in a bowl. Break it into smaller curds using a whisk or spoon, then stir in the salt.

Do not overcook or curds will be tough

recipes.title: Homemade Cream Cheese
recipes.source_note: Alphafoodie - alphafoodie.com
recipes.description: Super easy 3-ingredient cream cheese ready in 10 minutes. Light, fluffy, and perfect for spreading or baking.

instructions.text: Pour milk into a saucepan and bring to a gentle simmer over medium-high heat for 1-2 minutes. Avoid a full boil.
Add lemon juice and stir with a wooden spoon, then turn off heat.

Pour curdled milk through cheesecloth and a sieve to remove whey.
Rinse the curds with cold water.
Squeeze curds thoroughly to remove remaining whey (reserve whey for other uses if desired).
Place strained curds in a food processor or blender with salt. Blend until light and fluffy.
Add 1-2 tbsp whey while blending if you prefer creamier texture.
Enjoy immediately or refrigerate up to 7 days. Can be frozen up to 2 months.

Avoid vigorous stirring - it breaks up curds
Can customize with herbs, pepper, or sweet chili

recipes.title: Queso Fresco
recipes.source_note: Fias Co Farm - fiascofarm.com
recipes.description: Latin American semi-soft cheese that can substitute for mozzarella. Lightly pressed and ready to eat in just a few days.

ingredients.item: goat or cow milk (raw or pasteurized)

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F (90°F for cow milk). Add mesophilic culture and lipase, stir thoroughly.
Allow to ripen for 1 hour.
Dissolve rennet in water. Add to milk and stir vigorously for 15 seconds.
Cover and let sit 45 minutes until achieving a clean break, maintaining 86°F temperature.
Cut curds into 1/4-inch pieces. Rest undisturbed for 10 minutes.
Stir curds with wire whisk and gradually raise temperature to 95°F over 20 minutes, stirring occasionally. Let settle 5 minutes.
Drain whey (reserve for ricotta). Maintain curds at 95°F for 10 minutes while stirring.
Add salt and optional herbs (chives or jalapeños).
Line mold with cheesecloth. Add curds and press: 10 lbs for 10 minutes, flip, then 20 lbs for 1 hour, then 35 lbs for 6 hours.
Air dry overnight on a rack. Wrap and refrigerate several days before tasting.

recipes.description: Simple acid-set cheese also called vinegar cheese. Bland, rubbery texture that doesn't melt - ideal as a meat substitute in curries, chili, or tacos.

Does not melt - use as meat substitute

recipes.title: Homemade Mozzarella (Fias Co Farm)

recipes.description: Traditional stretched-curd mozzarella using citric acid for acidity development. Not recommended for beginners - the stretching technique takes practice.

ingredients.item: fresh goat or cow milk (not homogenized)

instructions.text: Sterilize all equipment. Pour milk into double boiler and add citric acid.

Dissolve rennet in water. Add to milk and stir briskly for 15 seconds, then stop milk movement.

Cut curds into 1/4-1/2 inch pieces using vertical, crosswise, then 45° angle cuts.

Don't answer phone during curd working phase

recipes.title: No-Rennet Queso Blanco
recipes.source_note: New Mexico State University Extension - pubs.nmsu.edu
recipes.description: Heat-acid white cheese made without culture or rennet. Semi-hard frying cheese that doesn't melt. Can be flavored with peppers, herbs, and spices.

recipes.title: SAFE Queso Fresco

recipes.title: Feta-Style Fresh Cheese
recipes.source_note: New Mexico State University Extension - pubs.nmsu.edu
recipes.description: Fresh feta-style cheese with hot brine treatment. Can be eaten fresh or aged, and seasoned with herbs, chile, or spices.

recipes.title: Neufchâtel Cheese

recipes.title: Pizza Cheese (Mozzarella)

recipes.title: Homemade Cheddar Cheese
recipes.source_note: Homesteaders of America - homesteadersofamerica.com
recipes.description: Traditional cloth-bound cheddar with the signature cheddaring process. Ages from 4-6 weeks for mild to 3+ months for sharp flavor.

instructions.text: Warm milk to 88°F, remove from heat.

recipes.title: Homemade Gouda Cheese

Stir gently for 12 minutes.

Add more water until curds reach 95°F.
Stir 10 minutes. Drain completely.
Transfer curds to mold.
Press at 15 lbs for 30 minutes, flip, press another 30 minutes.
After 12 hours, submerge in refrigerated brine overnight.
Remove, pat dry, place on mat at room temperature.
Turn regularly until dry (about 5 days).
Vacuum seal or wax.
Age minimum 2 months at 50-55°F with 75-95% humidity.

notes: Gouda's defining feature is its natural sweetness from the washing step

Wax or vacuum seal for aging

recipes.title: Traditional Gouda Cheese
recipes.source_note: Curd Nerd - curd-nerd.com
recipes.description: A traditional washed-curd gouda with proper pressing weights and extended aging. Features Flora Danica culture for authentic flavor.

instructions.text: Warm milk to 32°C (90°F).
Add Flora Danica culture and stir thoroughly.
Cover and ripen for 15 minutes.
Add diluted rennet and let set 45 minutes to 1 hour until clean break achieved.
Cut curds into 1cm cubes.
Rest 10 minutes.
Pour off one-third of whey.
Slowly add 80°C (175°F) water until temperature reaches 33°C (92°F).
Stir continuously, rest 10 minutes.
Drain whey to curd level.
Add more 80°C water until reaching 38°C (100°F).
Rest 30 minutes.
Drain all remaining whey.
Transfer curds gently to cloth-lined mold (avoid breaking curds).
Press at 10kg for 30 minutes; flip and redress.
Press at 20kg for 30 minutes; flip and redress.
Press at 25kg for 12 hours.
Unwrap cheese.
Soak in saturated brine 12 hours, turning every 3 hours.
Pat dry and air dry at 10°C for 3 weeks.
Wax and age at 10°C for 3-9 months.
Turn cheese 3-4 times weekly during aging.

notes: Flora Danica culture provides authentic Dutch flavor
Increasing press weights (10kg, 20kg, 25kg) develops proper texture
Turn cheese frequently during aging
Cheese improves with longer aging - patience pays off

recipes.title: Homemade Halloumi Cheese
recipes.source_note: Wholesome Cook - wholesome-cook.com
recipes.description: A quick halloumi using the microwave method. Ready in about an hour. Features the traditional herbs and high melting point for grilling.

instructions.text: Combine both milks in a large saucepan.
Dissolve the junket tablet in 1 tablespoon water.
Heat milk to 32-35°C (89.5-95°F), then remove from heat and add dissolved junket. Stir briefly.
Set aside for 30 minutes in a warm place. The milk should set and become jelly-like.
Cut the set milk into curds using a wooden spoon to separate the whey.
Transfer to a microwave-safe bowl with herbs and chilli. Wait 10 minutes.
Microwave on high for 2 minutes, stir, then heat another 2 minutes.
Test curds—they should be elastic and slightly firm. Heat 1 more minute if needed.
Line a fine sieve with gauze over a bowl. Strain curds, reserving 1/2 cup whey for brine.
Sprinkle salt over curds, mix, and press to remove excess whey.
Gather gauze edges and squeeze additional whey out.
Combine all brine ingredients and mix well.
Press cheese into a rectangular container. Refrigerate or freeze 15 minutes to cool.
Transfer to a larger container and cover with brine. Store in refrigerator for a couple of days.

notes: Halloumi has a high melting point - perfect for grilling or frying
Mix of cow and goat milk is traditional
Store in brine to preserve
Best grilled or pan-fried while fresh

recipes.title: Homemade Blue Cheese
recipes.source_note: Curd Nerd - curd-nerd.com
recipes.description: An advanced blue cheese using Penicillium Roqueforti. Requires needling to create characteristic blue veins. Ages 90+ days.

instructions.text: Warm milk to 30°C (86°F).
Add cultures (mesophilic and Penicillium Roqueforti) and stir thoroughly.
Ripen for 1.5 hours.
Add diluted rennet and let set for 1 hour until clean break achieved.
Carefully cut the curd into fine, pea-sized pieces.
Over 60 minutes, stir the curds every 5 minutes while maintaining temperature.
Drain curds through cheesecloth.
Salt the curds and transfer to molds.
Turn molds every 15 minutes for the first hour, then hourly for three more hours.
Store overnight at 80% humidity and 20°C.
For the next 14 days, rotate and turn the cheese stack daily at 95% humidity and 10°C.
Rub with salt for the first week only.
After 4-10 days of visible mold, pierce the cheese with a stainless-steel needle at 2.5cm intervals.
This needling creates air holes allowing oxygen inside, forming the characteristic blue veins.
Ripen for 90 additional days at 95% humidity and 10°C.
Turn every 3-4 days and scrape surface mold.
Finally, wrap in foil and store at 8°C.

notes: Advanced recipe - not for beginners
Needling is critical: pierce at 2.5cm intervals to allow oxygen penetration
The blue veins form along needle paths where oxygen enters
Only a tiny speck of Penicillium Roqueforti is needed
95% humidity is essential during aging

recipes.title: Brie de Meaux
recipes.source_note: Classic French cheesemaking tradition from Île-de-France region.

Cheese is ripe when it yields to gentle pressure

recipes.title: Comté (French Gruyère)

recipes.title: Milawa Blue-Style Cheese

instructions.text: Dice dried figs finely. Set aside.
Heat goat's milk to 72°F. Add culture, stir.
Add rennet drops in 2 tbsp water. Stir briefly.
Cover and let set 12-24 hours until thick.
Ladle into cheesecloth-lined colander. Drain 12-24 hours.
Add salt, drizzle honey, and fold in figs.
Mix gently. Form into log or rounds.
Drizzle with additional honey if desired.

notes: Use quality honey - flavor comes through
Dried figs add chewy texture and sweetness
Excellent with crackers and wine
Best served at room temperature

recipes.title: Caramelized Onion Cheddar
recipes.source_note: Modern British artisan cheese with deeply caramelized onions.
recipes.description: A sharp cheddar with sweet caramelized onions throughout. Savory and slightly sweet.

instructions.text: Slice onions thinly. Caramelize in butter over low heat 45-60 min until deep brown.
Cool caramelized onions completely. Chop finely.
Heat milk to 86°F. Add culture, ripen 45 min.
Add calcium chloride if needed, then rennet. Let set 45 min.
Cut curd into 1/2-inch cubes. Heat to 102°F over 40 min.
Cheddar curds for 2 hours.
Mill curds. Add reduced salt (onions are sweet) and onions. Mix.
Pack into mold. Press at 50 lbs for 24 hours.
Vacuum seal. Age at 55°F for 3-6 months.

notes: Take time to properly caramelize onions - don't rush
Onions must be cooled and chopped finely
Sweet onions balance sharp cheddar
Vacuum seal due to onion moisture

recipes.title: Apricot Stilton
recipes.source_note: Modern British combination of Stilton with dried apricots.
recipes.description: A creamy Stilton-style blue with dried apricot pieces. Sweet-savory and complex.

instructions.text: Dice dried apricots finely. Set aside.
Heat milk to 86°F. Add cultures. Ripen 1 hour.
Add calcium chloride if needed, then rennet. Let set 90 min.
Cut curd into 1/2-inch cubes.
Drain whey slowly. Salt curds with apricots. Mix gently.
Pack loosely into cylindrical mold.
Flip daily for 4-5 days at room temperature.
Pierce with needles after 5 weeks.
Age at 55°F with 90% humidity for 8-12 weeks.

notes: Apricot sweetness contrasts with blue tang
Orange apricot pieces visible throughout
Sweet-savory combination is addictive
Excellent with dessert wines

recipes.title: Manchego al Pimentón (Smoked Paprika Manchego)
recipes.source_note: Modern Spanish artisan cheese with characteristic smoked paprika.
recipes.description: A firm sheep's milk cheese with smoked Spanish paprika. Deep red color and smoky flavor.

instructions.text: Heat sheep's milk to 86°F. Add culture, ripen 30 min.
Add calcium chloride if needed, then rennet. Let set 45 min.
Cut curd into 1/4-inch pieces. Heat to 104°F over 30 min.
Drain whey. Add paprika and salt. Mix thoroughly.
Pack into traditional pleita mold.
Press at 30 lbs for 12 hours.
Rub rind with olive oil mixed with paprika.
Age at 50-55°F for 2-6 months.

notes: Use quality smoked paprika (pimentón de la Vera)
Cheese will have reddish-orange hue
Smoky flavor without actual smoking
Rind rubbed with paprika-oil adds color

recipes.title: Vintage Cheddar (24-Month Aged)
recipes.source_note: Extended aging for complex, crystalline cheddar.
recipes.description: A deeply aged cheddar with sharp, complex flavor and crunchy tyrosine crystals throughout.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F (30°C). Add culture. Ripen 45-60 minutes for extra acid development.
Add calcium chloride if needed, then rennet. Let set 45 minutes until very firm.
Cut curd into 3/8-inch cubes. Rest 5 minutes.
Slowly heat to 102°F (39°C) over 45 minutes, stirring gently.
Drain whey. Cheddar the curds for 2-3 hours (longer cheddaring = sharper cheese).
Mill curds into thumb-sized pieces. Salt thoroughly.
Pack tightly into mold. Press at 50 lbs for 24 hours.
Bandage wrap with cheesecloth and lard.
Age at 55°F (13°C) with 85% humidity for full 24 months.
Turn twice weekly. Repair bandage as needed.

notes: Extended cheddaring develops sharper flavor
Bandage wrapping essential for long aging
Tyrosine crystals develop after 18+ months
Color deepens to golden amber with age

recipes.title: Parmigiano-Style Stravecchio (36-Month)
recipes.source_note: Extra-aged Parmesan style for maximum complexity.
recipes.description: Ultra-aged Parmesan-style cheese with intense umami, crumbly texture, and abundant crystals.

instructions.text: Combine skimmed evening milk with whole morning milk. Heat to 91°F (33°C).
Add culture or whey starter. Ripen 15 minutes.
Add rennet. Let set 12 minutes until firm.
Break curd into rice-grain pieces using whisk.
Heat rapidly to 131°F (55°C) over 15 minutes, stirring constantly.
Let curds rest on bottom under whey for 50-60 minutes.
Lift curd mass with cloth. Place in large wheel mold.
Press with increasing weight for 2-3 days.
Brine for 20-25 days, turning daily.
Age at 60-68°F (15-20°C) with 80% humidity for full 36 months.
Turn and brush weekly throughout aging.

notes: Stravecchio means 'extra old' - minimum 36 months
Intensely umami with caramel and nutty notes
Crumbles rather than slices
White crystals (tyrosine) are prized

recipes.title: Overjarig Gouda (48-Month Extra-Aged)
recipes.source_note: Maximum aging for Dutch Gouda - extremely rare.
recipes.description: The rarest aged Gouda with intense butterscotch flavor and crunchy crystalline texture.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 90°F (32°C). Add culture. Ripen 30 minutes.
Add calcium chloride if needed, then rennet. Let set 45 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/2-inch cubes. Rest 5 minutes.
Remove 1/3 whey. Add hot water (150°F) to raise temp to 102°F (39°C).

Press at 30 lbs for 30 min, then 60 lbs for 24 hours.
Brine for 48 hours.
Air dry until rind is completely dry (5-7 days).
Wax with multiple thick layers.
Age at 50-55°F (10-13°C) with 85% humidity for full 48 months.
Check wax quarterly and repair any cracks.

notes: Overjarig means 'over-aged' - 4+ years
Develops intense butterscotch and caramel flavors
Extremely firm with abundant crystals
Color becomes deep amber/orange

recipes.title: Manchego Gran Reserva (18-Month)
recipes.source_note: Maximum aging classification for Manchego cheese.
recipes.description: The oldest classification of Manchego with intense, sharp flavor and crumbly texture.

instructions.text: Heat sheep's milk to 86°F (30°C). Add culture. Ripen 30 minutes.
Add calcium chloride if needed, then lamb rennet. Let set 45-60 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/4-inch pieces (rice-sized).
Heat to 104°F (40°C) over 30 minutes, stirring constantly.
Continue stirring until curds are very firm.
Drain whey. Pack tightly into traditional pleita mold.
Press at 30 lbs for 2 hours, then 50 lbs for 24 hours.
Dry salt rind or brine for 24 hours.
Age at 50-55°F (10-13°C) with 85% humidity for full 18 months.
Rub with olive oil weekly to maintain rind.

notes: Gran Reserva is the longest-aged Manchego classification
Sharp, complex, slightly spicy flavor
Becomes hard and crumbly
Dark brown-black rind develops naturally

recipes.title: Pule-Style Donkey Milk Cheese
recipes.source_note: Inspired by rare Serbian donkey cheese - one of world's most expensive.
recipes.description: An extremely rare, crumbly white cheese made from donkey milk. Requires large quantities of milk.

instructions.text: Donkey milk has very low casein - requires goat milk to help curd form.
Combine milks. Heat to 95°F (35°C).
Add rennet. Let set 60-90 minutes - curd will be very soft.
Gently ladle fragile curds into cheesecloth.
Let drain very gently 4-6 hours. Do not press.
Salt lightly. Shape into small rounds.
Refrigerate. Eat fresh within 1 week.

notes: Donkey milk is very low in fat and casein
Yield is extremely low - 25 liters milk per kg cheese
Authentic pule costs $500-1000+ per pound
Goat milk helps form curd structure

recipes.title: Moose Cheese (Älgost)
recipes.source_note: Rare cheese made at Elk House farm in Sweden.
recipes.description: An extremely rare white cheese made from moose milk. Rich and creamy.

instructions.text: Moose milk is very rich (10% fat, 10% protein). Handle gently.
Heat milk to 90°F (32°C). Add culture. Ripen 30 minutes.
Add rennet. Let set 45-60 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/2-inch cubes. Let rest 10 minutes.
Gently stir for 20 minutes.
Drain whey. Salt curds lightly.
Pack into small mold. Press gently.
Age at 55°F (13°C) for 2-4 months.

notes: Only one farm in the world (Elk House, Sweden) makes this commercially
Moose only lactate May-September
Yields about 300 kg total per year worldwide
Costs approximately $500+ per pound

recipes.title: Caravane (Camel Milk Cheese)
recipes.source_note: Developed with FAO assistance for Mauritanian herders.
recipes.description: A soft, fresh cheese made from camel milk using special techniques for this difficult-to-curdle milk.

instructions.text: Camel milk lacks kappa-casein found in cow milk - requires special handling.
Add calcium chloride to cold milk. Stir well.
Heat milk to 95°F (35°C).
Add camel chymosin or vegetable rennet. Let set 60-90 minutes.
Curd will be softer than cow milk cheese.
Cut gently. Let rest 15 minutes.
Drain through cheesecloth very gently.
Salt and shape. Eat fresh or age briefly.

notes: Camel milk has different protein structure than cow milk
Special camel chymosin enzyme developed for this purpose
Lower yield than cow milk cheese
Important food security cheese in desert regions

recipes.title: Reindeer Milk Cheese (Sámi Tradition)
recipes.source_note: Ancient Sámi herding tradition from northern Scandinavia.
recipes.description: A rich, creamy cheese made from reindeer milk. Very high in fat and protein.

instructions.text: Reindeer milk is extremely rich (22% fat, 10% protein).
Heat milk to 90°F (32°C). Add culture. Ripen 20 minutes.
Add rennet. Let set 30-45 minutes.
Cut curd into 1-inch cubes.
Gently stir for 15 minutes.
Drain whey. Salt curds.
Pack into small mold. Press lightly.
Can eat fresh or age 2-4 weeks for firmer texture.

notes: Reindeer milk is twice as rich as cow milk
Sámi people have herded reindeer for thousands of years
Very small yield - reindeer produce little milk
Rich, creamy flavor unlike any other cheese

recipes.title: Casu Marzu-Style (Fly Larvae Fermented Cheese)
recipes.source_note: Traditional Sardinian cheese. EDUCATIONAL ONLY - banned in many jurisdictions.

Place in wooden box with rye flour and existing cheese mite colony.

recipes.title: Chhurpi Soft (Himalayan Yak Cheese)

instructions.text: Yak milk is very rich (6-7% fat, 5% protein).
Heat milk to 180°F (82°C).
Add lemon juice or sour whey. Stir gently.
Curds will form and separate from whey.
Strain through cloth. Let drain 1-2 hours.
Salt and mix. Shape into rounds or squares.
Eat fresh (soft chhurpi) or dry for hard chhurpi.

notes: Yak milk is richer than cow milk

recipes.title: Mozzarella di Bufala Campana DOP
recipes.source_note: DOP protected authentic water buffalo mozzarella from Campania.
recipes.description: The original mozzarella - made from Italian water buffalo milk. Creamy, tangy, and porcelain white.

instructions.text: Buffalo milk is richer than cow milk (8% fat vs 3.5%).
Heat milk to 95°F (35°C). Add whey starter or citric acid.
Let ripen 30 minutes if using whey starter.

Cut curd. Let rest, then cut again into smaller pieces.
Let curds acidify until stretchy (pH 5.2, about 3-5 hours).
Heat water to 175°F (80°C). Stretch curds until smooth and elastic.
Form into balls. Drop in cold salted water to firm.
Store in light brine. Best within 24-48 hours.

notes: Authentic only from water buffalo in specific Italian regions
Whiter, creamier, more tangy than cow milk mozzarella

recipes.title: Provolone Mandarone (Giant Aged Provolone)

Add calcium chloride if needed, then rennet. Let set 30-40 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/2-inch cubes. Heat to 118°F (48°C).

Stretch in 175°F (80°C) water until very smooth.
Form into giant pear shape (mandarone means 'big mandarin').
Tie with rope at narrow end for hanging.
Brine for 1 week for large size.
Hang to dry 1 month, then age 2-3+ years hanging in cool cellar.

notes: Traditional shapes: mandarone (pear), salami, pancetta (slab)
Can weigh 50+ kg for commercial versions
Kid or lamb rennet essential for piquant flavor
Develops intense sharpness and crystals with age

recipes.title: Époisses (Marc-Washed Burgundy Cheese)
recipes.source_note: AOC protected. The 'king of cheeses' according to Brillat-Savarin.

Age at 55°F (13°C) with 95% humidity.

Continue washing 5-8 weeks. Rind becomes orange-red and very sticky.

Serve at room temperature in its traditional wooden box

recipes.title: Mozzarella Affumicata (Smoked Mozzarella)
recipes.source_note: Classic Neapolitan smoked mozzarella using straw burning
recipes.description: Creamy stretched-curd mozzarella with a brown smoked exterior and delicate wood smoke flavor throughout.

Cut curd into 1-inch cubes. Heat to 105°F while gently stirring.

Cold smoke using wheat straw (traditional) or fruit wood at 60-75°F for 2-4 hours.
Rest overnight in refrigerator before serving. Use within 1 week.

notes: Traditional affumicata uses wheat straw for smoking, giving a distinctive sweet smoke
Can also use fruit woods like apple or pear
Smoke fresh mozzarella within 24 hours of making for best results

recipes.title: Scamorza Affumicata (Smoked Scamorza)
recipes.source_note: Classic aged smoked Italian pasta filata cheese

Age hanging for 1-2 weeks before use.

recipes.title: Smoked Idiazábal

Cut curd into 1/4-inch pieces. Rest 5 minutes.
Slowly raise temperature to 100°F over 30 minutes, stirring constantly.
Hold at 100°F for 30 minutes more until curds are firm.
Drain whey and press curds into molds at 15 lbs for 1 hour.

Air dry for 2-3 days until natural rind forms.

Beech and cherry wood are traditional for Basque smoking

Natural rind develops a beautiful dark amber color from smoking

recipes.title: Ricotta Affumicata (Smoked Ricotta)
recipes.source_note: Sicilian and Calabrian smoked ricotta for grating
recipes.description: Dense, firm smoked ricotta with brown exterior, used for grating over pasta like ricotta salata but with smoky depth.

instructions.text: Heat fresh whey (and milk if using) to 185-195°F, stirring occasionally.
Add vinegar or lemon juice. Stir gently and watch for flocculation.
Remove from heat and let curds rise for 5-10 minutes.
Skim curds gently and place in ricotta basket or cheesecloth-lined mold.
Let drain at room temperature for 2-4 hours.
Salt all surfaces generously. Place in mold and weight lightly.
Refrigerate and drain for 2-3 days, salting surfaces daily.
Air dry at 55-60°F for 5-7 days until firm exterior develops.
Cold smoke with fruit wood at 65-75°F for 3-4 hours.
Continue aging at 55°F for 2-4 weeks. Grate like Parmesan over pasta.

recipes.temperature: 185-195°F for make; 65-75°F for smoking; 55°F for aging
notes: Use fresh whey within a few hours of cheesemaking for best yield
The longer you drain and salt, the firmer the final cheese
Excellent grated over pasta e fagioli or eggplant dishes

recipes.title: Smoked Blue Cheese
recipes.source_note: Modern American artisan smoked blue cheese technique
recipes.description: Creamy, tangy blue cheese with subtle cold smoke flavor that complements the Penicillium complexity.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F. Add mesophilic culture and P. roqueforti. Ripen 1 hour.
Add calcium chloride, then rennet. Set for 90 minutes until firm.
Cut curd into 1/2-inch cubes. Let rest 5 minutes.
Gently stir for 15 minutes at 86°F. Do not heat further.
Drain whey. Ladle curds gently into molds without pressing.
Let drain naturally, turning every 30 minutes for 4-6 hours.
Dry salt all surfaces. Let absorb for 24 hours.
Pierce wheel with sanitized skewers to create air channels for blue development.
Age at 55°F and 95% humidity for 2-3 months, turning weekly.
Once blue veins are well developed, cold smoke at 60-70°F for 2-3 hours.
Age 2-4 more weeks after smoking for flavors to meld.

recipes.temperature: 86°F for make; 60-70°F for smoking; 55°F for aging
notes: Smoke only after blue is well developed
Light smoking preserves blue cheese character
Pairs excellently with bacon and steak

recipes.title: Smoked Brie
recipes.source_note: Artisan smoked soft-ripened cheese technique
recipes.description: Creamy, buttery Brie with light applewood smoke and bloomy white rind, an elegant appetizer cheese.

instructions.text: Combine milk and cream. Heat to 72°F. Add all cultures. Ripen 1 hour.
Add calcium chloride, then rennet. Set at 72°F for 12-18 hours.
Gently ladle curds into Brie molds without breaking. Let drain naturally.
Turn molds every 2-3 hours for the first day.
Once firm, remove from molds and salt all surfaces.
Age at 55°F and 95% humidity for 10-14 days until white mold covers surface.
Cold smoke very lightly at 50-60°F for 1-2 hours maximum.
Wrap in cheese paper and continue aging at 45°F for 2-4 more weeks.
Serve when center is soft and oozy.

recipes.temperature: 72°F for make; 50-60°F for smoking; 45-55°F for aging
notes: Very light smoking only - the delicate Brie flavor should remain dominant
Smoke before full ripening so mold can recover
The rind will brown slightly from smoke but white mold should remain

recipes.title: Smoked Swiss Emmental
recipes.source_note: Traditional Emmental with beechwood smoking
recipes.description: Sweet, nutty Emmental with characteristic eyes and subtle beechwood smoke, excellent for fondue and sandwiches.

Add calcium chloride if using, then rennet. Set for 25-30 minutes.
Cut curd into rice-sized pieces (1/8 inch). Rest 5 minutes.
Slowly raise temperature to 125°F over 1 hour, stirring constantly.
Hold at 125°F for 30 minutes until curds are very firm.
Drain and press at 10 lbs for 30 min, then 30 lbs for 6 hours.
Brine in saturated salt solution for 24-36 hours.
Age at 55°F for 2 months, washing with brine weekly.
Move to 70°F 'warm room' for 3-4 weeks for eye development.
Return to 55°F. After 4+ months aging, cold smoke with beechwood at 70-80°F for 4-6 hours.
Continue aging to 8 months for best flavor.

recipes.temperature: 90-125°F for make; 70-80°F for smoking; 55-70°F for aging
notes: The warm room phase is essential for eye development
Larger wheels develop better flavor
Smoke enhances the sweet, nutty character

recipes.title: Hickory Smoked Cheddar
recipes.source_note: Bold American-style smoked cheddar with intense hickory flavor
recipes.description: Sharp, tangy cheddar with bold, bacon-like hickory smoke flavor, perfect for burgers and mac and cheese.

Add calcium chloride, then rennet. Set for 45 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/4-inch cubes. Rest 5 minutes.
Slowly raise to 102°F over 30 minutes, stirring constantly.
Hold at 102°F for 30 more minutes until curds are firm and squeaky.
Drain whey. Mill curds into finger-sized pieces. Salt and mix.
Press at 10 lbs 15 min, 20 lbs 30 min, 50 lbs overnight.
Air dry at room temperature for 3-5 days until rind forms.
Age at 55°F for minimum 3 months.
Cold smoke with hickory at 70-85°F for 6-8 hours over 2 days.
Rest 2 weeks, then continue aging for 3-12 months total.

recipes.temperature: 86-102°F for make; 70-85°F for smoking; 55°F for aging

The smoke flavor intensifies with aging

recipes.title: Smoked Monterey Jack

Press at 10 lbs for 15 min, then 25 lbs for 6-8 hours.
Air dry for 2-3 days until slight rind forms.
Age at 55°F for minimum 4 weeks.
Cold smoke with mesquite at 70-80°F for 4-6 hours.

recipes.temperature: 88-100°F for make; 70-80°F for smoking; 55°F for aging
notes: Mesquite gives a distinctly Southwestern character
Monterey Jack's mild flavor lets the smoke shine
Excellent melting properties for cooking

recipes.title: Garlic and Herb Cream Cheese (Boursin Style)
recipes.source_note: Homemade version of the famous French garlic and herb cheese
recipes.description: Rich, creamy fresh cheese with garlic, herbs, and cracked black pepper, perfect for spreading on crackers or bread.

Add diluted rennet. Stir gently and cover.
Let set at room temperature for 12-24 hours until thick like yogurt.
Line colander with butter muslin. Gently ladle curds into cloth.
Tie corners and hang to drain for 12-24 hours until thick and spreadable.
Transfer drained cheese to bowl. Add salt and mix well.
Add garlic, chives, parsley, thyme, and pepper. Mix thoroughly.
Pack into molds or roll into logs. Refrigerate overnight.
Store refrigerated for up to 2 weeks.

notes: Use fresh herbs for best flavor
Can substitute dried herbs at 1/3 the amount
Excellent rolled in additional herbs or crushed peppercorns

recipes.title: Dill Havarti
recipes.source_note: Classic Danish Havarti with fresh dill throughout
recipes.description: Creamy, buttery Havarti studded with fresh dill, perfect for sandwiches and Scandinavian dishes.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F. Add mesophilic culture. Ripen 30 minutes.
Add calcium chloride, then rennet. Set for 45 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/2-inch cubes. Let rest 10 minutes.
Gently stir for 10 minutes, then let curds settle.
Remove 1/3 of whey. Add 170°F water to raise temperature to 100°F.
Stir at 100°F for 15 minutes until curds are springy.
Drain most whey. Add chopped dill and mix thoroughly with curds.
Press at 8 lbs for 30 min, 15 lbs for 2 hours.
Brine for 8-12 hours in saturated salt solution.
Air dry for 2-3 days, then wax or vacuum seal.
Age at 55°F for 2-3 months.

notes: Fresh dill is essential - dried dill doesn't work as well
Can also make caraway Havarti using 2 tbsp caraway seeds
The dill flavor intensifies with aging

recipes.title: Sage Derby
recipes.source_note: Historic English cheese with sage leaves creating green marbling
recipes.description: Mild, mellow Derby cheese with distinctive green marbling from sage leaves, a British Christmas tradition.

instructions.text: Blend sage (and spinach if using) with 1 cup of the milk until smooth green liquid.
Strain through fine mesh, pressing to extract all green juice.
Heat remaining milk to 86°F. Add culture and ripen 30 minutes.
Add calcium chloride, then rennet. Set for 45 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/2-inch cubes. Rest 5 minutes.
Slowly raise to 94°F over 30 minutes, stirring gently.
Drain whey and divide curds in half. Add sage juice to one half, mixing well.
Layer plain and green curds alternately in mold for marbled effect.
Press at 10 lbs for 15 min, 30 lbs for 4-6 hours.
Salt all surfaces. Air dry for 3-5 days.
Age at 55°F for 1-3 months, turning weekly.

notes: Traditional Sage Derby uses only sage juice for green color
Spinach boosts the green color without affecting flavor
The marbled pattern makes beautiful slices
Traditional Christmas cheese in England

recipes.title: Cumin Gouda (Komijnekaas)
recipes.source_note: Classic Dutch Gouda with cumin seeds (Leidse kaas style)
recipes.description: Creamy Dutch Gouda studded with aromatic cumin seeds, a traditional Leiden specialty.

instructions.text: Toast cumin seeds in dry pan until fragrant. Set aside to cool.
Heat milk to 86°F. Add mesophilic culture. Ripen 45 minutes.
Add calcium chloride, then rennet. Set for 45 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/2-inch cubes. Rest 5 minutes.
Slowly raise to 100°F over 30 minutes, stirring gently.
Remove 1/3 of whey. Replace with 175°F water. This washes the curds.
Stir at 100°F for 20 minutes until curds are firm.
Drain whey. Add toasted cumin seeds and mix thoroughly.
Press at 10 lbs for 30 min, flip, then 20 lbs for 2 hours.
Brine for 8-12 hours in saturated salt solution.
Air dry 2-3 days. Wax and age at 55°F for 2-6 months.

notes: Toasting the cumin brings out more flavor
Traditional Leiden cheese also adds caraway
Excellent with dark bread and mustard

recipes.title: Lavender Honey Chèvre
recipes.source_note: Aromatic fresh goat cheese with lavender and honey
recipes.description: Delicate fresh goat cheese infused with culinary lavender and drizzled with local honey, a Provençal delicacy.

instructions.text: Heat goat milk to 72°F. Add mesophilic culture. Stir and let ripen 1 hour.
Add diluted rennet. Stir gently for 30 seconds.
Cover and let set at room temperature for 18-24 hours until thick.
Gently ladle curds into cheesecloth-lined molds.
Let drain 24-48 hours until desired consistency.
Unmold cheese and add salt, mixing gently.
Crush lavender buds slightly and fold into cheese.
Form into logs or rounds. Drizzle with honey before serving.
Store refrigerated for up to 10 days.

notes: Use only culinary-grade lavender (pesticide-free)
Herbes de Provence can substitute for lavender
Pairs beautifully with fresh fruit and crusty bread

recipes.title: Nettle Gouda (Brandnetelkaas)
recipes.source_note: Dutch Gouda with stinging nettles giving green flecks and earthy flavor
recipes.description: Creamy Gouda with distinctive green flecks from stinging nettles, offering a subtle earthy, spinach-like flavor.

instructions.text: Wearing gloves, blanch nettles in boiling water for 2 minutes. Drain, squeeze dry, and chop fine.
Heat milk to 86°F. Add mesophilic culture. Ripen 45 minutes.
Add calcium chloride, then rennet. Set for 45 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/2-inch cubes. Rest 5 minutes.
Slowly raise to 100°F over 30 minutes, stirring gently.
Remove 1/3 whey. Replace with 175°F water. Continue stirring 20 minutes.
Drain whey. Add prepared nettles to curds and mix thoroughly.
Press at 10 lbs for 30 min, flip, then 20 lbs for 2 hours.
Brine for 8-12 hours.
Air dry 2-3 days. Wax and age at 55°F for 2-4 months.

notes: Always blanch nettles first to remove sting
Spring nettles have the best flavor
Can substitute spinach if nettles unavailable

recipes.title: Fenugreek Gouda
recipes.source_note: Dutch Gouda with fenugreek seeds for maple-like sweetness
recipes.description: Creamy Gouda studded with fenugreek seeds that add a distinctive maple and curry-like aroma.

instructions.text: Lightly crush fenugreek seeds to release flavor.
Heat milk to 86°F. Add mesophilic culture. Ripen 45 minutes.
Add calcium chloride, then rennet. Set for 45 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/2-inch cubes. Rest 5 minutes.
Slowly raise to 100°F over 30 minutes, stirring gently.
Remove 1/3 whey. Replace with 175°F water. Continue stirring 20 minutes.
Drain whey. Add fenugreek seeds and mix thoroughly.
Press at 10 lbs for 30 min, flip, then 20 lbs for 2 hours.
Brine for 8-12 hours.
Air dry 2-3 days. Wax and age at 55°F for 2-4 months.

notes: Fenugreek has a distinctive maple-curry aroma
Popular in Dutch and German cheesemaking
Pairs well with Indian and Middle Eastern cuisines

recipes.title: Rosemary Manchego
recipes.source_note: Traditional Manchego pressed with fresh rosemary
recipes.description: Firm, buttery Manchego with aromatic rosemary pressed into the rind and throughout, perfect with Spanish wines.

instructions.text: Heat sheep's milk to 86°F. Add thermophilic culture. Ripen 45 minutes.
Add calcium chloride if using, then rennet. Set for 30-45 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/4-inch pieces. Rest 5 minutes.
Slowly raise to 104°F over 30 minutes, stirring constantly.
Hold at 104°F for 30 more minutes until curds are firm.
Drain whey. Add minced rosemary to curds and mix.
Line mold with rosemary sprigs. Add curds and press.
Press at 10 lbs for 30 min, flip, then 25 lbs for 6-8 hours.
Dry salt by rubbing salt on all surfaces for 24 hours.
Rub with olive oil. Age at 55°F for 2-6 months.

notes: The rosemary sprigs create beautiful imprint on rind
Traditional Manchego uses esparto grass molds
Pairs wonderfully with membrillo (quince paste)

recipes.title: Black Pepper Pecorino (Pecorino al Pepe)
recipes.source_note: Tuscan/Roman sheep's milk cheese with cracked black pepper
recipes.description: Sharp, tangy sheep's milk cheese with generous cracked black pepper throughout and coating the rind.

instructions.text: Heat sheep's milk to 90°F. Add thermophilic culture. Ripen 30 minutes.
Add calcium chloride if using, then rennet. Set for 30-45 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/2-inch cubes. Rest 5 minutes.
Slowly raise to 116°F over 45 minutes, stirring constantly.
Hold at 116°F for 15 minutes until curds are quite firm.
Drain whey. Add half the cracked pepper to curds and mix.
Press at 15 lbs for 1 hour, flip, then 30 lbs for 6-8 hours.
Dry salt all surfaces. Age 1-2 days.
Coat exterior with remaining cracked pepper, pressing into rind.
Age at 55°F for 2-8 months, turning weekly.

notes: Use high-quality peppercorns for best flavor
The pepper flavor intensifies with aging
Essential for authentic cacio e pepe pasta

recipes.title: Époisses de Bourgogne (Burgundy Wine-Washed)
recipes.source_note: Famous French washed-rind cheese washed with Marc de Bourgogne
recipes.description: Pungent, creamy washed-rind cheese with sticky orange rind from washings with Marc de Bourgogne brandy.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F. Add mesophilic culture and B. linens. Ripen 1 hour.
Add calcium chloride, then rennet. Set for 90 minutes.
Gently ladle curds into Époisses molds without breaking.
Let drain naturally 24 hours, turning every 6 hours.
Salt all surfaces. Let cure 24 hours.
Move to aging cave at 55°F and 95% humidity.
Mix Marc with equal parts light brine. Wash cheese every 2-3 days.
Continue washing and aging for 6-8 weeks until rind is sticky orange and interior is soft.
Wrap in paper and store refrigerated. Serve at room temperature.

notes: Marc de Bourgogne is grape pomace brandy - substitute cognac if unavailable
The smell is strong but the flavor is complex and mild
One of France's most famous (and pungent) cheeses
Banned on public transport in France due to its aroma!

recipes.title: Port Wine Washed Cheese
recipes.source_note: Semi-soft cheese with ruby Port wine wash creating deep purple rind
recipes.description: Creamy semi-soft cheese with beautiful purple-stained rind from Port wine washings and subtle grape sweetness.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F. Add mesophilic culture and B. linens. Ripen 45 minutes.
Add calcium chloride, then rennet. Set for 45 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/2-inch cubes. Rest 5 minutes.
Slowly raise to 98°F over 30 minutes, stirring gently.
Drain whey. Press at 10 lbs for 30 min, flip, then 20 lbs for 4 hours.
Salt all surfaces. Age at 55°F and 90% humidity.
After 1 week, begin washing with Port wine every 2-3 days.
Continue washing for 4-8 weeks until rind is deep purple and cheese is semi-soft.

notes: Ruby Port gives the deepest color; tawny works too
The alcohol evaporates but the grape flavor remains
Beautiful centerpiece for cheese boards

recipes.title: Beer-Washed Cheese (Bierkäse)
recipes.source_note: Semi-soft cheese washed with Belgian-style ale
recipes.description: Pungent, meaty washed-rind cheese with complex flavors from beer washings, perfect with crusty bread.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 90°F. Add mesophilic culture and B. linens. Ripen 30 minutes.
Add calcium chloride, then rennet. Set for 45 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/2-inch cubes. Rest 5 minutes.
Slowly raise to 100°F over 30 minutes, stirring gently.
Drain whey. Press at 10 lbs for 30 min, flip, then 20 lbs for 4 hours.
Brine for 4-6 hours in saturated salt solution.
Age at 55°F and 95% humidity.
After 1 week, begin washing with beer every 2-3 days.
Continue washing for 6-10 weeks until rind is sticky and orange-brown.

notes: Belgian abbey ales and German doppelbock work excellently
The beer contributes yeast and malt flavors
Pairs perfectly with the same beer used for washing

recipes.title: Irish Whiskey Cheddar
recipes.source_note: Sharp Irish cheddar soaked in Irish whiskey
recipes.description: Sharp, crumbly Irish cheddar infused with Irish whiskey, offering warm, oaky notes with vanilla undertones.

instructions.text: Make cheddar using standard method: heat milk to 86°F, add culture, ripen 45 min.
Add calcium chloride and rennet. Set 45 minutes.
Cut curd 1/4-inch. Heat slowly to 102°F over 30 minutes.
Hold at 102°F for 30 minutes until curds are firm and squeaky.
Drain whey. Mill curds and salt. Press overnight at 50 lbs.
Age cheddar at 55°F for minimum 3 months.
Cut aged wheel into quarters. Soak in Irish whiskey for 24-48 hours.
Remove, pat dry, and wrap. Age 1-2 more weeks for flavors to meld.
Alternatively: Brush wheel with whiskey weekly during final month of aging.

notes: Jameson or Powers work well for this
The whiskey flavor mellows with additional aging
A wonderful after-dinner cheese with Irish coffee

recipes.title: Grappa-Washed Italian Cheese (Ubriaco)
recipes.source_note: Aged Italian cheese soaked in grape marc and grappa
recipes.description: Firm, tangy cheese aged in grape skins and washed with grappa, with distinctive purple color and winey flavor.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 95°F. Add thermophilic culture. Ripen 30 minutes.
Add calcium chloride and rennet. Set 30-45 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/2-inch cubes. Slowly raise to 110°F over 30 minutes.
Drain whey. Press at 20 lbs for 30 min, flip, then 40 lbs for 6 hours.
Brine for 12-24 hours.
Age at 55°F for minimum 2 months.
Mix grape marc with grappa. Bury cheese in the marc mixture.
Store covered at 55°F for 2-4 months, turning occasionally.
Remove from marc. The rind will be deep purple. Age 2 more weeks before serving.

notes: Ubriaco means 'drunken' in Italian
Red wine grape marc gives the most color
The cheese absorbs wine and fruit flavors from the marc
Traditional in the Veneto region during grape harvest

recipes.title: Calvados-Washed Camembert
recipes.source_note: Classic Normandy Camembert washed with apple brandy
recipes.description: Rich, creamy Camembert with bloomy rind brushed with Calvados apple brandy, adding fruity complexity.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 90°F. Add mesophilic culture, P. candidum, and G. candidum. Ripen 90 minutes.
Add calcium chloride if using, then rennet. Set for 90 minutes.
Carefully ladle curds into Camembert molds. Let drain overnight.
Turn molds several times during draining.
Salt all surfaces. Let drain 1 more day.
Move to aging cave at 55°F and 95% humidity.
After white mold appears (7-10 days), brush with Calvados every 3-4 days.
Continue aging and occasional Calvados washing for 4-6 weeks.
Cheese is ready when center feels soft when pressed.

notes: Calvados is essential for authentic Norman flavor
American apple brandy or applejack can substitute
The apple notes pair beautifully with the mushroomy Camembert

recipes.title: Cider-Washed Farmhouse Cheese
recipes.source_note: Traditional farmhouse cheese washed with hard cider
recipes.description: Semi-soft farmhouse cheese with sticky orange rind from cider washings, offering tangy apple notes.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 88°F. Add mesophilic culture and B. linens. Ripen 45 minutes.
Add calcium chloride, then rennet. Set for 45 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/2-inch cubes. Rest 5 minutes.
Slowly raise to 100°F over 30 minutes, stirring gently.
Drain whey. Press at 10 lbs for 30 min, flip, then 20 lbs for 4 hours.
Brine for 6-8 hours.
Age at 55°F and 95% humidity.
After 1 week, begin washing with hard cider every 2-3 days.
Continue washing for 6-10 weeks until rind is sticky and orange.

notes: Use a dry, tannic farmhouse cider
The cider adds tartness and subtle apple flavor
Perfect with more hard cider or perry

recipes.title: Mead-Washed Honey Cheese
recipes.source_note: Artisan cheese washed with honey wine (mead)
recipes.description: Golden semi-soft cheese washed with mead, offering subtle honey sweetness and floral complexity.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F. Add mesophilic culture and B. linens. Ripen 45 minutes.
Add calcium chloride, then rennet. Set for 45 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/2-inch cubes. Rest 5 minutes.
Slowly raise to 98°F over 30 minutes, stirring gently.
Drain whey. Press at 10 lbs for 30 min, flip, then 20 lbs for 4 hours.
Brine for 6-8 hours.
Age at 55°F and 95% humidity.
After 1 week, begin washing with mead every 2-3 days.
Continue washing for 6-8 weeks until rind develops golden-orange color.

notes: Use a semi-sweet or traditional mead
The honey sugars feed the rind bacteria
Excellent with fresh fruit and honey

recipes.title: Cranberry Wensleydale
recipes.source_note: Traditional English Wensleydale with dried cranberries
recipes.description: Crumbly, mild Wensleydale studded with sweet-tart dried cranberries, a festive British favorite.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 84°F. Add mesophilic culture. Ripen 1 hour.
Add calcium chloride if using, then rennet. Set for 60 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/2-inch cubes. Rest 5 minutes.
Gently stir for 40 minutes at 84°F. Do not heat further.
Drain whey. Gently break curds by hand and add salt.
Add chopped cranberries and mix thoroughly.
Gently press at 5 lbs for 15 min, then 10 lbs for 4-6 hours.
Air dry for 2-3 days at room temperature.
Wax and age at 55°F for 3-6 weeks.

notes: Traditional Christmas cheese in the UK
The mild cheese lets the cranberry flavor shine
Can also make blueberry or apricot versions

recipes.title: Fig and Walnut Goat Cheese
recipes.source_note: Fresh chèvre rolled in dried figs and toasted walnuts
recipes.description: Tangy fresh goat cheese rolled in a coating of chopped dried figs and crunchy toasted walnuts.

instructions.text: Heat goat milk to 72°F. Add mesophilic culture. Stir and let ripen 1 hour.
Add diluted rennet. Stir gently for 30 seconds.
Cover and let set at room temperature for 18-24 hours until thick.
Gently ladle curds into cheesecloth-lined molds.
Let drain 24-48 hours until desired consistency.
Unmold and add salt, mixing gently.
Form into logs. Mix chopped figs and toasted walnuts together.
Roll cheese logs in fig-walnut mixture, pressing gently to adhere.
Wrap and refrigerate. Store up to 2 weeks.

notes: Toast walnuts in 350°F oven for 8-10 minutes for best flavor
Can substitute pecans or hazelnuts
Beautiful holiday appetizer

recipes.title: Apricot Stilton
recipes.source_note: White Stilton with dried apricots
recipes.description: Creamy, crumbly white Stilton studded with sweet dried apricots, a popular English dessert cheese.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F. Add mesophilic culture. Ripen 1 hour.
Add calcium chloride if using, then rennet. Set for 90 minutes.
Gently cut curd into 1/2-inch cubes. Rest 5 minutes.
Stir gently at 86°F for 30 minutes. Let curds settle.
Ladle curds into cheesecloth-lined mold. Let drain 30 minutes.
Turn cheese. Continue draining for 6-8 hours, turning every hour.
Remove from mold. Salt all surfaces.
Break cheese into pieces, add diced apricots, and reform in mold.
Age at 55°F and 90% humidity for 4-8 weeks.

notes: White Stilton has no blue mold - it's a separate cheese
Apricot Stilton is a protected name in the UK
Also popular: mango, lemon, or ginger Stilton

recipes.title: Pistachio-Crusted Chèvre
recipes.source_note: Fresh goat cheese rolled in crushed pistachios
recipes.description: Creamy fresh goat cheese with a crunchy bright green pistachio coating, elegant for entertaining.

instructions.text: Heat goat milk to 72°F. Add mesophilic culture. Stir and let ripen 1 hour.
Add diluted rennet. Stir gently for 30 seconds.
Cover and let set at room temperature for 18-24 hours.
Gently ladle curds into cheesecloth-lined molds.
Let drain 24-48 hours until firm enough to handle.
Unmold and add salt, mixing gently.
Form into logs or rounds.
Roll cheese in finely chopped pistachios, pressing gently.
Refrigerate at least 2 hours before serving.

notes: Use unsalted pistachios for best control of seasoning
The bright green color is stunning on a cheese board
Can add a drizzle of honey when serving

recipes.title: Date Gouda
recipes.source_note: Creamy Gouda studded with Medjool dates
recipes.description: Buttery Dutch Gouda with sweet, caramel-like Medjool dates throughout, perfect for dessert courses.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 86°F. Add mesophilic culture. Ripen 45 minutes.
Add calcium chloride, then rennet. Set for 45 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/2-inch cubes. Rest 5 minutes.
Slowly raise to 100°F over 30 minutes, stirring gently.
Remove 1/3 whey. Replace with 175°F water. Stir 20 minutes.
Drain whey. Add chopped dates and mix thoroughly.
Press at 10 lbs for 30 min, flip, then 20 lbs for 2 hours.
Brine for 8-12 hours.
Air dry 2-3 days. Wax and age at 55°F for 2-4 months.

notes: Medjool dates give the best caramel-like sweetness
The dates create pockets of sweetness in each bite
Excellent with strong coffee or after dinner drinks

recipes.title: Hazelnut Toma (Toma alle Nocciole)
recipes.source_note: Piedmontese Toma cheese with local hazelnuts
recipes.description: Creamy Italian Toma studded with toasted Piedmont hazelnuts, celebrating the region's famous nuts.

instructions.text: Toast hazelnuts at 350°F for 10-12 minutes. Rub in towel to remove skins. Chop coarsely.
Heat milk to 90°F. Add mesophilic culture. Ripen 30 minutes.
Add calcium chloride, then rennet. Set for 45 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/2-inch cubes. Rest 5 minutes.
Slowly raise to 100°F over 30 minutes, stirring gently.
Drain whey. Add toasted hazelnuts to curds and mix.
Salt curds and press at 15 lbs for 30 min, then 30 lbs for 6 hours.
Air dry for 3-5 days.
Age at 55°F for 2-4 months, turning weekly.

notes: Piedmont hazelnuts (nocciole) are considered the world's finest
Toasting brings out the nutty flavor essential for this cheese
Pairs beautifully with Barolo wine

recipes.title: Wild Blueberry Chèvre
recipes.source_note: Fresh goat cheese with wild Maine blueberries
recipes.description: Tangy fresh goat cheese swirled with wild blueberry compote, creating beautiful purple marbling.

instructions.text: Make blueberry compote: simmer blueberries with honey until thickened. Cool completely.
Heat goat milk to 72°F. Add mesophilic culture. Ripen 1 hour.
Add diluted rennet. Stir gently for 30 seconds.
Cover and let set at room temperature for 18-24 hours.
Gently ladle curds into cheesecloth-lined molds.
Let drain 24-48 hours until firm.
Unmold and add salt and lemon zest, mixing gently.
Fold in cooled blueberry compote to create swirls - don't fully mix.
Form into logs or rounds. Refrigerate.

notes: Wild blueberries have more intense flavor than cultivated
The marbling effect is beautiful when sliced
Serve with honey and crusty bread

recipes.title: Toasted Pecan Cheddar
recipes.source_note: Sharp cheddar studded with Southern pecans
recipes.description: Sharp, tangy cheddar with crunchy toasted pecans throughout, a Southern twist on classic cheddar.

instructions.text: Toast pecans at 350°F for 8-10 minutes until fragrant. Cool and chop.
Heat milk to 86°F. Add culture. Ripen 45 minutes.
Add calcium chloride if using, then rennet. Set 45 minutes.
Cut curd into 1/4-inch cubes. Rest 5 minutes.
Slowly raise to 102°F over 30 minutes, stirring constantly.
Hold at 102°F for 30 minutes until curds are firm and squeaky.
Drain whey. Mill curds into finger-sized pieces.
Add salt and toasted pecans. Mix thoroughly.
Press at 10 lbs 15 min, 20 lbs 30 min, 50 lbs overnight.
Air dry 3-5 days. Wax and age at 55°F for 3-12 months.

notes: Southern pecans have a richer, more buttery flavor
The pecans add texture contrast to the sharp cheddar
Excellent with apple slices and bourbon

recipes.title: Valençay (Ash-Ripened Pyramid)
recipes.source_note: Classic French goat cheese pyramid dusted with vegetable ash
recipes.description: Tangy French goat cheese in truncated pyramid shape, coated with edible vegetable ash under bloomy white rind.

instructions.text: Heat goat milk to 72°F. Add mesophilic culture, P. candidum, and G. candidum. Ripen 1 hour.
Add diluted rennet. Stir gently. Cover and set at room temperature for 18-24 hours.
Gently ladle curds into Valençay pyramid molds.
Let drain naturally 24-48 hours, turning once.
Unmold when firm. Salt all surfaces.
Let salt absorb for 24 hours.
Dust all surfaces with food-grade vegetable ash.
Age at 55°F and 90% humidity for 3-5 weeks until white mold covers the ash.
Cheese is ready when it gives slightly when pressed.

notes: Legend says Napoleon sliced off the top point after his Egyptian defeat
The ash neutralizes surface acid and promotes mold growth
Food-grade ash is made from burning grape vines or vegetables

recipes.title: Banon (Chestnut Leaf-Wrapped)
recipes.source_note: Small French goat cheese wrapped in chestnut leaves soaked in eau-de-vie
recipes.description: Soft, creamy Provençal goat cheese wrapped in brandy-soaked chestnut leaves tied with raffia.

instructions.text: Soak chestnut leaves in eau-de-vie for at least 2 hours.
Heat goat milk to 72°F. Add mesophilic culture. Ripen 1 hour.
Add diluted rennet. Set at room temperature for 18-24 hours.
Gently ladle curds into small round molds (about 3 inches).
Let drain 24-48 hours until firm.
Unmold and salt all surfaces. Let dry for 1-2 days.
Wrap each cheese in 3-4 overlapping chestnut leaves. Tie with raffia.
Age at 55°F for 2-4 weeks. The leaves will slowly brown.
Interior should be soft and creamy when ready.

notes: Grape leaves can substitute for chestnut if unavailable
The leaves contribute subtle tannins and flavor
Traditional autumn/winter cheese in Provence

recipes.title: Cave-Aged Gruyère (Reserve)
recipes.source_note: Extended cave-aged Swiss Gruyère for maximum complexity
recipes.description: Intensely flavored Swiss Gruyère aged 18+ months in natural caves, with crystalline texture and deep nutty taste.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 90°F. Add thermophilic culture (and Propionibacterium if using). Ripen 15 minutes.
Add calcium chloride if using, then rennet. Set 30-40 minutes.
Cut curd into rice-sized pieces. Rest 5 minutes.
Stir and slowly raise temperature to 120°F over 45 minutes.
Hold at 120°F, stirring for 30-45 minutes until curds are firm.
Drain and press at 25 lbs for 30 minutes, flip, then 50 lbs overnight.
Brine in saturated salt solution for 24 hours.
Age at 55°F, washing rind with brine weekly for first 3 months.
Move to cave (or cave-like conditions: 54°F, 95% humidity) for extended aging.
Continue aging minimum 18 months, ideally 24 months, for reserve quality.

notes: Extended aging develops tyrosine crystals that add crunch
Reserve Gruyère is PDO protected - must age in specific caves
The flavor becomes more complex and nutty with age

recipes.title: Paneer (Indian Fresh Cheese)
recipes.source_note: Simple acid-set fresh cheese essential to Indian cuisine
recipes.description: Firm, mild fresh cheese that holds its shape when cooked, essential for palak paneer and other Indian dishes.

instructions.text: Heat milk to 185-190°F, stirring occasionally to prevent scorching.
Remove from heat. Add lemon juice, stirring gently.
Let sit 10 minutes. Curds should separate from clear whey.
If not fully separated, add more acid, 1 tbsp at a time.
Line colander with cheesecloth. Pour curds and whey through.
Rinse curds under cold water to remove acid taste.
Add salt if desired. Gather cheesecloth and squeeze out excess moisture.
Place wrapped paneer on plate. Top with heavy weight.
Press 1-2 hours until firm. Cut into cubes for cooking.

notes: Paneer doesn't melt, making it perfect for curries
Fresh paneer is soft; pressed paneer is firm for frying
Use within 3-4 days refrigerated
